title: The Project Brief
instruction: Choose the option that best reflects senior LXD judgement.

_items.text: Evaluate which design framework fits this context — ADDIE, SAM, or Agile — before doing anything else
_items._feedback: Starting with a framework evaluation is strategic — you chose based on context, not habit. This is what senior LXD practitioners do: diagnose before prescribing.

_items.text: Jump straight to evaluation standards — define how you'll measure success before you design anything
_items._feedback: Jumping to evaluation too early skips a critical step. Without a framework, you have no process to evaluate against. Define your approach first, then your metrics.

_items.text: Skip the planning phase entirely and jump into building a quick prototype to show stakeholders
_items._feedback: Prototyping without a plan is a common risk. In a 3-week project, this leads to scope creep. Always start with a framework decision.

_feedback.title: Feedback
_feedback.correct: Strong choice. Evaluating frameworks first sets a strategic direction before diving into tactics.
_feedback._correct: Strong choice. Evaluating frameworks first sets a strategic direction before diving into tactics.

_incorrect.notFinal: Defining success metrics early or prototyping is good practice, but starting with a design framework provides the structure needed to keep this 3-week project on track.
_incorrect.final: In LXD, the framework guides every decision that follows. Starting without one leads to misalignment and rework.

body: You are a Learning Experience Designer at EdTech Corp...

title: Choosing Your Design Framework
instruction: Choose the framework that best fits the timeline.

_items.text: ADDIE — Analyze, Design, Develop, Implement, Evaluate. The full waterfall approach.
_items._feedback: ADDIE's linear waterfall is too rigid for a 3-week sprint. You would spend half the project in Analysis alone.

_items.text: SAM (Successive Approximation Model) — iterative prototyping with frequent stakeholder reviews.
_items._feedback: SAM's 'savvy start' lets you prototype rapidly and refine through stakeholder feedback. Ideal for tight deadlines where quality still matters.

_items.text: Dick & Carey Model — the systems-oriented approach with 10 sequential components.
_items._feedback: Dick & Carey is thorough but over-engineered for a 3-week compliance course. Too much front-end analysis for the timeline.

_items.text: Agile / LLAMA — full iterative development with minimal up-front design.
_items._feedback: Agile works well for software but can skip critical learner analysis in LXD. SAM offers a better balance for this context.

_feedback.title: Feedback
_feedback.correct: Strong choice! SAM's iterative 'savvy start' approach lets you prototype quickly and refine based on feedback — perfect for tight timelines without sacrificing quality.
_feedback._correct: Strong choice! SAM's iterative 'savvy start' approach lets you prototype quickly and refine based on feedback — perfect for tight timelines without sacrificing quality.

_incorrect.notFinal: For a 3-week compliance project, SAM (Successive Approximation Model) typically provides the best balance of rigor and speed. ADDIE and Dick & Carey are too linear; Agile may skip needed analysis.
_incorrect.final: For a 3-week compliance project, SAM (Successive Approximation Model) typically provides the best balance of rigor and speed.

title: The Analysis Dilemma
displayTitle: How do you handle the PM's request?
instruction: Choose the response that demonstrates senior LXD practice.

_items.text: Push back respectfully — explain that without a learner analysis, you risk building a course that doesn't address the actual performance gaps across different departments
_items._feedback: You advocated for the learner and the process — that's senior LXD leadership. A targeted 2-day analysis sprint addresses the PM's timeline while gathering critical data.

_items.text: Accept the PM's shortcut but plan a quick survey during development to gather learner data retroactively
_items._feedback: A retroactive survey won't capture the performance gaps you need to design for. Push back with a lighter-weight analysis plan instead.

_items.text: Propose a full ADDIE analysis phase including stakeholder interviews, job observation, and performance metrics review
_items._feedback: A full ADDIE analysis is overkill for a 3-week timeline. Propose a targeted 2-day sprint: stakeholder interviews plus a quick learner survey.

_feedback.title: Feedback
_feedback.correct: Excellent. This is the mark of a senior LXD — advocating for the learner while demonstrating business acumen.
_feedback._correct: Excellent. This is the mark of a senior LXD — advocating for the learner while demonstrating business acumen.

_incorrect.notFinal: Analysis must happen before design decisions. A targeted 2-day analysis sprint would satisfy both the PM and your quality standards.
_incorrect.final: Skipping analysis is a common but costly shortcut. A targeted 2-day analysis sprint would satisfy both the PM and your quality standards.

title: Evaluation Strategy
instruction: Choose the level that best demonstrates behavior change.

_items.text: Level 1: Reaction — Did learners enjoy the course? Use smile sheets and satisfaction surveys.
_items._feedback: Smile sheets show satisfaction, not behavior change. For proving workplace impact, you need Level 3 (Behavior) or higher.

_items.text: Level 2: Learning — Did learners acquire the knowledge? Use pre/post test scores.
_items._feedback: Test scores prove learning occurred, not whether it transferred to the job. Behavior change requires Level 3.

_items.text: Level 3: Behavior — Are learners applying data privacy practices on the job? Use observation, manager reports, or audit data.
_items._feedback: Level 3 is where you prove the training changed workplace practices — through audits, manager observations, or performance data.

_feedback.title: Feedback
_feedback.correct: Correct. Level 3 is where you demonstrate actual workplace behavior change — the gold standard for compliance training ROI.
_feedback._correct: Correct. Level 3 is where you demonstrate actual workplace behavior change — the gold standard for compliance training ROI.

_incorrect.notFinal: For behavior change, you need Kirkpatrick Level 3 (Behavior) — observable application on the job through audits, manager observations, or performance data.
_incorrect.final: For behavior change, you need Kirkpatrick Level 3 (Behavior) — observable application on the job through audits, manager observations, or performance data.

title: Formative vs Summative
instruction: Choose the evaluation type that fits this situation.

_items.text: Formative evaluation — analyze the pilot data, identify knowledge gaps, revise content, and re-test before full launch
_items._feedback: Formative evaluation is exactly right. You are in development with data that needs action. Fix it now before 500+ employees see it.

_items.text: Summative evaluation — launch as planned and measure the final outcome at the end, treating 60% as your baseline
_items._feedback: Launching with a 60% pass rate is premature. Formative evaluation lets you diagnose and fix gaps in the remaining 2 weeks.

_items.text: Phillips ROI evaluation — calculate the monetary return on investment based on projected improvement from the pilot data
_items._feedback: Phillips ROI is premature here. You need to fix the learning intervention first before measuring its financial return.

_feedback.title: Feedback
_feedback.correct: Perfect. Formative evaluation during development lets you fix problems before they reach the full audience.
_feedback._correct: Perfect. Formative evaluation during development lets you fix problems before they reach the full audience.

_incorrect.notFinal: Formative evaluation is the right call here. Use the remaining 2 weeks to analyze, revise, and re-pilot before going live.
_incorrect.final: Formative evaluation is the right call here. Use the remaining 2 weeks to analyze, revise, and re-pilot before going live.

title: Proving Value
instruction: Choose the best evaluation approach for this request.

_items.text: Kirkpatrick Level 4: Results — report organizational impact metrics like reduced data breaches or improved audit scores
_items._feedback: Level 4 shows organizational impact but doesn't produce the monetary ROI percentage the VP needs for the board.

_items.text: Phillips ROI Methodology — convert benefit data into monetary values, subtract program costs, and calculate the ROI percentage
_items._feedback: Phillips ROI converts benefits to dollar values and calculates a clear percentage. This is exactly what the VP needs for the board presentation.

_items.text: CIPP Model — evaluate Context, Input, Process, and Product to give a holistic picture of program value
_items._feedback: CIPP provides a holistic evaluation but doesn't produce the hard monetary ROI figure the VP is asking for.

_feedback.title: Feedback
_feedback.correct: Perfect. Phillips ROI is specifically designed for the scenario where leadership needs a hard dollar figure.
_feedback._correct: Perfect. Phillips ROI is specifically designed for the scenario where leadership needs a hard dollar figure.

_incorrect.notFinal: For a direct monetary ROI figure, Phillips ROI Methodology is the appropriate framework. It isolates the training's financial contribution and presents it as a clear percentage.
_incorrect.final: For a direct monetary ROI figure, Phillips ROI Methodology is the appropriate framework. It isolates the training's financial contribution and presents it as a clear percentage.

title: Scenario Complete
body:
Congratulations! You have completed the LXD Design Frameworks & Evaluation Standards branching scenario.

Below is a detailed breakdown of every decision you made, the correct choice, and why it matters.

Loading your decisions...

title: Global Rollout Challenges
instruction: Choose the option that best reflects senior LXD judgement.

_items.text: Translate the existing course exactly as-is into each language. Delivering on time is the priority — we can fix cultural issues in v2.
_items._feedback: Launching culturally insensitive content damages credibility. Learners in Tokyo or Berlin will disengage immediately. Always localize meaning, not just words.

_items.text: Redesign the course for each locale with local SMEs: adapt examples, replace US-specific case studies, and run cultural sensitivity reviews. This will push the timeline but ensures quality.
_items._feedback: This is best practice. Localizing at the cultural level ensures every learner feels the content was designed for them. Delaying quality global content is always worth it.

_items.text: Replace all text with icons and visuals so it's 'culture-free.' That way you don't need translation at all.
_items._feedback: There is no such thing as 'culture-free' design. Visuals carry cultural meaning too — colors, symbols, gestures, and even layouts vary across cultures. Always involve local SMEs.

_feedback.title: Feedback
_feedback.correct: You recognized that true localization means adapting meaning, not just language. Senior LXD practitioners design for cultural context, not just linguistic accuracy.
_feedback._correct: You recognized that true localization means adapting meaning, not just language. Senior LXD practitioners design for cultural context, not just linguistic accuracy.

_incorrect.notFinal: Global rollout requires more than translation. Local SMEs help you adapt examples, case studies, and cultural references so the content resonates in each market.
_incorrect.final: Global rollout requires more than translation. Local SMEs help you adapt examples, case studies, and cultural references so the content resonates in each market.

title: Recovering from a Misstep
instruction: Choose the option that best reflects senior LXD judgement.

_items.text: Apologize for the oversight, take full ownership, and present a revised plan with local SME involvement in each region.
_items._feedback: Owning the mistake and presenting a concrete fix demonstrates senior leadership. Stakeholders trust practitioners who are honest and solution-oriented.

_items.text: Explain that the 'original intent was good' and ask the local teams to 'fix the language themselves since they know their culture best.'
_items._feedback: Delegating your core responsibility to local teams undermines your role as an LXD professional. You own the learning experience globally.

_items.text: Defend the original approach, citing the tight timeline as justification for the missteps.
_items._feedback: Defensiveness erodes trust. Stakeholders value honesty and ownership over excuses. Acknowledging the error builds credibility for future collaboration.

_feedback.title: Feedback
_feedback.correct: Ownership and transparency build long-term trust. Senior LXDs treat mistakes as data — they analyze, adjust, and communicate with honesty.
_feedback._correct: Ownership and transparency build long-term trust. Senior LXDs treat mistakes as data — they analyze, adjust, and communicate with honesty.

_incorrect.notFinal: When a rollout goes wrong, the strongest response is ownership + a clear plan. Defensiveness or blame-shifting erodes your credibility as an LXD leader.
_incorrect.final: When a rollout goes wrong, the strongest response is ownership + a clear plan. Defensiveness or blame-shifting erodes your credibility as an LXD leader.

title: Microlearning vs Deep Dive
instruction: Choose the option that best reflects senior LXD judgement.

_items.text: Agree immediately — the CLO is the boss, and microlearning is a trend for a reason. Deliver 9 x 5-minute chunks.
_items._feedback: Blindly following trends without evidence undermines learning outcomes. Microlearning works for awareness-level content, not for complex topics requiring deep understanding.

_items.text: Push back with evidence: research shows complex compliance topics require deeper processing. Propose a blended approach — microlearning for awareness, scenario-based deep dives for application.
_items._feedback: Evidence-based persuasion is a hallmark of senior LXD practice. You balanced stakeholder desire with learning science — the blended approach is the gold standard here.

_items.text: Propose a compromise: make the first 15 minutes microlearning-style and keep the remaining 30 minutes as a deep dive. Split the difference.
_items._feedback: Compromising on structural integrity can create a disjointed experience. Better to design a coherent blend from the ground up rather than cut an existing course into pieces.

_feedback.title: Feedback
_feedback.correct: Perfect. You used evidence to guide the stakeholder while offering a better solution. Senior LXDs are trusted advisors, not order-takers.
_feedback._correct: Perfect. You used evidence to guide the stakeholder while offering a better solution. Senior LXDs are trusted advisors, not order-takers.

_incorrect.notFinal: Microlearning has its place — but not for complex compliance topics. A blended approach that layers awareness-level chunks with deeper application scenarios is the evidence-backed solution.
_incorrect.final: Microlearning has its place — but not for complex compliance topics. A blended approach that layers awareness-level chunks with deeper application scenarios is the evidence-backed solution.

title: The Accessibility Audit
instruction: Choose the option that best reflects senior LXD judgement.

_items.text: Conduct a full WCAG 2.1 AA audit, fix all critical violations, and build an accessibility checklist for future projects.
_items._feedback: WCAG 2.1 AA is the industry standard. Fixing violations and building process safeguards prevents recurrence. This is what ethical LXD practice looks like.

_items.text: Fix the alt-text and colour contrast issues now. Tackle the rest in a future update.
_items._feedback: Partial fixes can still leave learners excluded. Keyboard traps and navigation issues are just as critical as alt-text. A comprehensive approach is the ethical minimum.

_items.text: Suggest the learner use a different screen reader and hope the compliance audit doesn't catch the rest.
_items._feedback: Passively shifting responsibility to the learner is unacceptable. Accessibility is not optional — it's a fundamental requirement of professional LXD practice.

_feedback.title: Feedback
_feedback.correct: Accessibility is non-negotiable in professional LXD. By fixing all violations and building safeguards, you ensure every learner can access the content with dignity.
_feedback._correct: Accessibility is non-negotiable in professional LXD. By fixing all violations and building safeguards, you ensure every learner can access the content with dignity.

_incorrect.notFinal: WCAG 2.1 AA compliance should be built in from the start, not retrofitted. Prioritize a comprehensive fix — partial accessibility still excludes learners.
_incorrect.final: WCAG 2.1 AA compliance should be built in from the start, not retrofitted. Prioritize a comprehensive fix — partial accessibility still excludes learners.

title: The Data Breach Incident
instruction: Choose the option that best reflects senior LXD judgement.

_items.text: Analyze the incident data: what knowledge gap did the breach expose? Use the findings to update the course with a targeted module on data handling protocols.
_items._feedback: This is continuous improvement in action. Treating incidents as data points — not failures — is what separates exceptional LXDs from average ones.

_items.text: Point to the 92% completion rate and positive feedback as proof the training worked. The breach was a human error, not a training failure.
_items._feedback: Completion rates and satisfaction scores don't prove behaviour change. True evaluation asks: did learners transfer the learning to their jobs? Use this as a diagnostic opportunity.

_items.text: Blame Finance for not enforcing your recommended follow-up workshops. The training was fine — it's the department that dropped the ball.
_items._feedback: Blame-shifting avoids accountability. A senior LXD practitioner owns the full learning ecosystem, including whether recommendations were implemented.

_feedback.title: Feedback
_feedback.correct: Excellent. You used the incident as a learning opportunity to close the loop. This is the essence of continuous improvement in LXD — data-driven iteration.
_feedback._correct: Excellent. You used the incident as a learning opportunity to close the loop. This is the essence of continuous improvement in LXD — data-driven iteration.

_incorrect.notFinal: A breach after training doesn't mean the training failed — it means the training needs iteration. Use incident data to identify specific gaps and update the course accordingly.
_incorrect.final: A breach after training doesn't mean the training failed — it means the training needs iteration. Use incident data to identify specific gaps and update the course accordingly.

title: Root Cause Analysis
instruction: Choose the option that best reflects senior LXD judgement.

_items.text: Conduct a performance analysis: interview the employee, observe the workflow, and identify environmental barriers (workflow, tools, culture) that prevented application.
_items._feedback: Performance analysis isolates whether the gap is a training problem or a workplace problem. Often, learners know what to do but workplace pressures override their training.

_items.text: Add 5 more knowledge-check questions to the existing course to 'deepen understanding.' If they pass again, the training is fine.
_items._feedback: More knowledge checks won't solve an application gap. The learner already passed the test — the issue is transfer to the job, not recall.

_items.text: Survey all 500+ employees asking 'did you apply what you learned?' and use the self-report data to guide revisions.
_items._feedback: Self-report surveys about application are unreliable. Learners overestimate their own application. Direct observation and workflow analysis are far more diagnostic.

_feedback.title: Feedback
_feedback.correct: Performance analysis reveals whether the gap is training or environment. This is advanced LXD practice — knowing that training alone rarely changes behaviour without workplace support.
_feedback._correct: Performance analysis reveals whether the gap is training or environment. This is advanced LXD practice — knowing that training alone rarely changes behaviour without workplace support.

_incorrect.notFinal: Root cause analysis separates training gaps from environmental barriers. Interview, observe, and analyse the workflow before jumping to a training solution.
_incorrect.final: Root cause analysis separates training gaps from environmental barriers. Interview, observe, and analyse the workflow before jumping to a training solution.

title: Modernizing the Approach
instruction: Choose the option that best reflects senior LXD judgement.

_items.text: Implement xAPI for rich activity tracking, and use the data to build personalized learning pathways that adapt to each learner's knowledge gaps.
_items._feedback: xAPI + adaptive pathways is the frontier of LXD. You've connected data, personalisation, and scalability in one strategic move.

_items.text: Stick with SCORM 1.2 — it's reliable, every LMS supports it, and upgrading risks compatibility issues.
_items._feedback: SCORM 1.2 is stable but limited. It can't track granular activities or support modern features like adaptive pathways. Upgrade to xAPI for richer data.

_items.text: Jump straight to VR training — immersive learning is the future, and this will position EdTech Corp as an innovator.
_items._feedback: VR without a clear learning need is trend-chasing. The data breach gap requires better knowledge application, not immersion. Start with xAPI and adaptive design.

_feedback.title: Feedback
_feedback.correct: Strategic vision + practical implementation = senior LXD leadership. xAPI unlocks data-driven personalization without betting the farm on unproven tech.
_feedback._correct: Strategic vision + practical implementation = senior LXD leadership. xAPI unlocks data-driven personalization without betting the farm on unproven tech.

_incorrect.notFinal: The right tech stack starts with the learning need, not the technology. xAPI provides the data layer needed for personalization while remaining practical and proven.
_incorrect.final: The right tech stack starts with the learning need, not the technology. xAPI provides the data layer needed for personalization while remaining practical and proven.

title: Strategic Reset
instruction: Choose the option that best reflects senior LXD judgement.

_items.text: Run a 2-day discovery sprint: interview learners, map current workflows, identify tech pain points, and prototype 3 solution options with estimated impact and cost.
_items._feedback: A discovery sprint is efficient and evidence-based. You'll have a data-backed recommendation ready within the VP's timeline.

_items.text: Research what competitors are using and recommend the most popular solution. If everyone is using it, it must be right.
_items._feedback: Copying competitors without understanding your own context leads to misaligned investments. Your learners' needs, not competitors' choices, should drive the decision.

_items.text: Recommend doing nothing for now — gather more data over the next 6 months before making any tech changes.
_items._feedback: Analysis paralysis is just as risky as impulsive decisions. A focused 2-day sprint gives you enough data for a confident recommendation.

_feedback.title: Feedback
_feedback.correct: A discovery sprint is the fastest path to a data-backed recommendation. You balanced urgency with rigour — exactly what senior LXDs do.
_feedback._correct: A discovery sprint is the fastest path to a data-backed recommendation. You balanced urgency with rigour — exactly what senior LXDs do.

_incorrect.notFinal: When the path forward is unclear, a structured discovery sprint (not analysis paralysis or copycat decisions) produces the most reliable roadmap.
_incorrect.final: When the path forward is unclear, a structured discovery sprint (not analysis paralysis or copycat decisions) produces the most reliable roadmap.

title: Building Your LXD Brand
instruction: Choose the option that best reflects senior LXD judgement.

_items.text: A transparent case study: show the ups, downs, data, failures, and lessons learned. Include the accessibility complaint, the breach incident, and how each challenge made the final product stronger.
_items._feedback: Authentic case studies build real credibility. Sharing failures as well as successes positions you as a grounded, reflective practitioner — exactly what the industry needs more of.

_items.text: A polished highlight reel: focus on the 96% satisfaction, the 92% completion rate, and the global rollout success. Keep it positive and inspiring.
_items._feedback: A highlight reel gets polite applause but little lasting impact. The audience learns more from your failures than your successes. Include the struggles.

_items.text: Decline the opportunity — you're too busy building the next project. Suggest the VP present it instead.
_items._feedback: Sharing your work at industry events builds your professional brand and elevates the LXD profession. It's not optional — it's part of being a senior practitioner.

_feedback.title: Feedback
_feedback.correct: Authenticity builds credibility. By sharing the full story — failures included — you model the reflective practice that defines senior LXD leadership.
_feedback._correct: Authenticity builds credibility. By sharing the full story — failures included — you model the reflective practice that defines senior LXD leadership.

_incorrect.notFinal: Industry presentations are opportunities to elevate the profession. The most respected presenters share their failures openly — the audience learns more from those than from highlight reels.
_incorrect.final: Industry presentations are opportunities to elevate the profession. The most respected presenters share their failures openly — the audience learns more from those than from highlight reels.

title: The LXD Career Crossroads
instruction: Choose the option that best reflects senior LXD judgement.

_items.text: Accept the Director role. Build a team that reflects your LXD values: evidence-based, learner-centered, and impact-driven. Your influence multiplies through others.
_items._feedback: Moving into leadership when you're ready is a service to the profession. Great LXDs become great leaders who create more great LXDs. This is how the field grows.

_items.text: Decline the Director role and stay hands-on. You love designing, and deep expertise matters as much as breadth. You'll continue to hone your craft and mentor informally.
_items._feedback: Staying hands-on is a valid, powerful choice. Deep expertise drives innovation, and informal mentoring still elevates the field. Not everyone needs to manage people to lead.

_items.text: Accept the Director role but keep designing everything yourself. You trust your own work more than anyone else's.
_items._feedback: Holding onto both roles leads to burnout and bottlenecks your team. Leadership means letting go of control and growing others. Delegate the design, lead the vision.

_feedback.title: Feedback
_feedback.correct: Whichever authentic path you chose, you're thinking strategically about your career. Senior LXDs know that growing the profession — through leadership OR deep expertise — is part of the job.
_feedback._correct: Whichever authentic path you chose, you're thinking strategically about your career. Senior LXDs know that growing the profession — through leadership OR deep expertise — is part of the job.

_incorrect.notFinal: Your career path should align with your strengths and values. Both hands-on expertise and leadership are vital to the LXD profession. The key is choosing consciously, not by default.
_incorrect.final: Your career path should align with your strengths and values. Both hands-on expertise and leadership are vital to the LXD profession. The key is choosing consciously, not by default.
